notes: Pipeline: (1) Perception: the head camera's depth image is turned into world points using the given intrinsics and extrinsics. Only points 4-80 mm above the table are kept. Cubes are picked out by colour ratios (r/g/b divided by their sum, so overall brightness doesn't matter). For each cube, the top-face points are fitted with a square: the code tries angles every 2° and keeps the one where the 2nd-98th percentile extents are smallest. That gives the centre and the yaw (mod 90°). It takes the median of 3 frames. Offline error on the practice frames was under 1 mm and about 1°. (2) Grasp planning: the grasp is top-down with the palm facing down, and the pinch axis (site x) lined up with a cube face. Up to 4 hand yaws (yaw + k·90°) are scored with a multi-seed damped-least-squares IK (pregrasp 12 cm above the cube, then the grasp pose). The score adds IK error, how close the joints are to their limits, arm collisions with the torso, table and bins (contacts checked in the private model), how close the finger and thumb paths come to the other cubes and the bin walls, and a mild preference for a natural hand yaw. The place pose above the target bin gets its own hand yaw, chosen the same way. (3) Motion: the moves to the pregrasp and to the bin follow joint-space paths that are corrected each step by IK onto a straight Cartesian line with interpolated yaw, using a smooth time profile. Descent and lift use per-step Cartesian IK. At the pregrasp, the wrist camera re-measures the cube's position and yaw at close range; the update is used only if it agrees with the head estimate. The fingers are pre-curled (closure 0.25) while descending so they sweep less, then closed fully, then the cube is lifted to 0.96 m. (4) Checking the grasp: after the lift and after the move to the bin, the cube counts as held if there are many target-coloured wrist pixels closer than 13 cm, or if the thumb is stopped by an object and the head camera no longer sees the cube on the table. If the check fails, the arm goes back to home, looks again, and retries (up to 4 attempts, avoiding hand yaws that already failed). (5) Placing: lower until the cube's bottom is about 3.5 cm above the table inside the bin, open, and retreat upward. On 120 practice episodes the last versions succeeded on about 97%. Known weaknesses: a cube right next to a bin with a diagonal yaw may be ungraspable without hitting the wall (seed 100008 fails: repeated failed grasps push the cube around). A failed grasp can occasionally knock a cube off the front edge of the table. The colour thresholds assume roughly neutral lighting. Robustness to camera calibration bias depends on the wrist-camera refinement.
